cards.explanation: The answer is that Samson tells them, "Now get her for me as a wife." He comes home from Timnah and says, "I have seen a daughter of the Philistines in Timnah. Now get her for me as a wife." No warm-up, no small talk. He walks in the door and goes straight to the request.

The answer is that they ask whether he can't find a wife among their own people. His father and mother ask, "Can’t you find a young woman among your relatives or among any of our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?" They ask it as two questions, one right after the other. I think they were hoping he'd say yes to the first one.

The answer is that this was from the LORD. The writer steps in with a side note: Samson's father and mother "…did not know this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines…" So there's more going on than a young man and what he likes. The LORD is working in it, and Samson's parents can't see that yet.

The answer is "ruling." The text says the LORD was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines, "for at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel." Israel had Philistines in charge of things. That's the situation the whole story sits in.

The answer is a young lion, friends. Samson's walking through the vineyards of Timnah when it comes roaring at him. I'd have started a brand new career in sprinting, gold base and all. The text keeps it simple: a young lion, and it's roaring.

The answer is that Samson tears the lion apart with his bare hands. The Spirit of the LORD comes powerfully upon him, and he tears the lion apart "…as one would tear a young goat." No weapon is mentioned at all. And this is the Spirit's doing, friends, not just a strong afternoon.

The answer is False. Judges 14:6 says he did not tell his father or mother what he had done. Samson tore a lion apart and then kept it to himself. Hold on to that, friends, because this secret is going to matter.

The answers are bees and honey, friends. Samson leaves the road to see the lion's carcass, and in it is a swarm of bees, "…along with their honey." That's an unexpected tenant. Samson scoops some into his hands and eats it as he goes. A lion and then honey, in the same story.
The answer is True. When Samson returns to his father and mother, he gives them some honey and they eat it. He eats his handful on the way, then shares with them. The part he leaves out comes next.

The answer is that he leaves out that he took it from the lion's carcass. The text says he "…did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass." His father and mother eat the honey he gives them, and he doesn't tell them where it came from. It's the second secret of the lion, friends.
The answer is thirty. When the Philistines saw Samson, they selected thirty men to accompany him. That's a big crowd, friends. And it matters for the bet that comes next.

The answer is thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes. Samson says, "If you can solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes." Thirty men, thirty garments, thirty sets. And if they can't solve it, they owe him the same.

The answer is the honey in the lion's carcass. The eater is the lion and the strong one is the lion. The something sweet is the honey Samson found in the carcass (Judges 14:8-9). And he never told his father and mother where that honey came from (Judges 14:9).

The answer is his wife. On the fourth day the men say to her, "Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death." That's a heavy thing to say to anyone. I think she was in a hard spot.

The answer is "You do not really love me." Weeping, she tells him, "You hate me! You do not really love me! You have posed to my people a riddle, but have not explained it to me." The riddle was a bet with her people, and she wanted the answer. Samson doesn't give it to her yet.
The answer is False. Judges 14:17 says she wept the whole seven days of the feast. On the seventh day, because she had pressed him so much, he finally told her the answer. It was a long week.

The answer is that she explains the riddle to her people. After Samson tells her, the text says "…in turn she explained the riddle to her people." She had been weeping for seven days, so I think that answer didn't stay put for long. Then, before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the city say to Samson, "What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?"

The answer is that he gives them to the men who solved the riddle. The text says Samson "…gave their clothes to those who had solved the riddle." So the bet gets paid. Still, this one is a heavy part, because it comes after he killed thirty men at Ashkelon.

The answer is True. After the clothes are handed over, the text says "…burning with anger, Samson returned to his father’s house…" The riddle, the pressure and the bet all end in anger. And his father's house is where he heads.

The answer is that she is given to one of the men who accompanied him. The text says, "…his wife was given to one of the men who had accompanied him." I think this one hurts, friends. Samson went home, and the story doesn't stay quiet about what happened next.
